findings.title: File-level selector is defined three incompatible ways
findings.description:
Correction 2 gives three definitions that do not agree:
- **Heading:** file-level means "carries a `filePath`".
- **Fix sentence:** "the file-level selector becomes an explicit type allow-list".
- **Next paragraph:** "Stated as an exclusion rather than an allow-list deliberately", with the selector `type != "function" and type != "class"`.

The architecture's read discipline enumerates nine file-level types as an allow-list. The deny-list inverts that default: any new upstream sub-file type (a `method` or `variable` node, say) is read automatically. The "no `filePath` → drift" guard only fires after the nodes have been selected, and only if the new type lacks `filePath`.

Pick one definition and delete the other two phrasings. If the deny-list stays, state that it deliberately departs from the architecture's enumerated list and why the context-blowup risk is acceptable.

findings.title: Dependency section reads function/class nodes that the read discipline forbids
findings.description:
Section 6 resolves "function- and class-level edge endpoints … to their owning file's layer". This conflicts with three statements:
- The architecture: "function- and class-level nodes are not read".
- Success Criterion 9 (line 333): "no function- or class-level node is read".
- Walkthrough step 7.

The resolution mechanism is also unstated (parse the type-prefixed `id`, follow `contains` edges, or read the node). The same paragraph first limits inter-layer connections to `imports` and `depends_on`, then counts a `calls` edge as an inter-layer signal.

Related gaps in the same row:
- "Ties by `weight`" (line 179) is undefined for an aggregated layer-pair count.
- `edges[].direction` is listed as consumed (line 86) but appears in no rule.
- `nodes[].tags` "section grouping" (line 84) is not used anywhere.

Lightest fix: restrict section 6 to edges whose endpoints are both file-level and drop the function/class resolution. Otherwise specify an id-only resolution and amend Criterion 9.

findings.title: Coverage reconciliation generalises a one-graph coincidence into an invariant
findings.description:
The design says file-level node count equal to `analyzedFiles` "is the expected case", and that a mismatch "means the graph is internally inconsistent". That was measured on a graph containing only `file`, `config` and `pipeline` nodes. The six other file-level types (`service`, `endpoint`, `schema`, `table`, `document`, `resource`) are not known to be one-per-analysed-file.

On an unfamiliar codebase, which is this slice's stated purpose, the generated document could tell readers a healthy graph is inconsistent. The same applies to two other claims:
- "Every file-level node belongs to exactly one layer (verified)" at line 218; the architecture guarantees this only for files.
- Section 6 has no stated handling for an endpoint with no layer membership.

The Risk Assessment covers single-graph risk for Correction 1 only. Report both numbers and the type breakdown without asserting inconsistency, and add a fallback for layer-less nodes.

findings.title: Closing observations are an unmarked-inference path
findings.description:
Each section carries a closing observation said to be "mechanically derivable" from the table above it. The design's own example fails that test: "complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK" is not derivable from `complexity`, `filePath` and `summary`.

Combined with Criterion 8 (zero `[INFERRED]` markers), interpretive claims would be emitted unmarked. That contradicts line 186 ("the fallback column has no third option") and the plan criterion that sections emit gap markers "rather than inferred prose". Cut the closing observations, or restrict them to restating counts from the table.

findings.title: Reading-order row drops `tour[].nodeIds`
findings.description:
The plan assigns this slice "`tour[]` ordering as the signal for which components matter most". The architecture says squadron "reads the tour as structured data with node IDs", and slice 363 attempts "`tour[]` node ordering" for Solution Approach.

Row 5 sources only `order`, `title` and `description`, so the section names no components. Slice 361's proving output did read `nodeIds`. Without them:
- the reading order cannot be checked against the repo, which is plan criterion 5;
- the mapping 363 reuses lacks the field it needs.

Add `nodeIds`, resolved to `filePath` for file-level members.

findings.title: `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` is "retained unchanged" and edited
findings.description: The design says the document "stays … unchanged, as the architecture requires" and then adds a cross-reference line to it. The Overview (line 22) also says everything is edits to `understand.md`. The plan asks only that the decision be recorded and the document remain in place. Drop the cross-reference line (and Criteria 7 and 11's mention of it), or stop saying "unchanged".

findings.title: Success criteria pin snapshot values
findings.description: Criteria 4 and 5 hardcode 34, 6 and 238. Walkthrough step 2 hardcodes index 944. The design itself notes "the graph may have been refreshed". State the criteria as relations (count equals `nodeIds | length`; selector count reconciles with `analyzedFiles`) and keep the numbers as walkthrough expectations only.

findings.title: Claims about the 361 skill text are not verifiable from the documents
findings.description: The corrections describe what the implemented 361 skill and the 943 sample say. The 361 slice design specifies `select(.type == "file" or ...)`, not a collapsed selector, and says nothing about mixed `nodeIds`; `commands/analysis/understand.md` is not present in this checkout and 361 is still `not_started`. Walkthrough step 1 re-measures the graph before implementing, which is adequate. The corrections sit in the comprehension flow that 362 "deepens in place", so they are in scope.

findings.title: Scope, boundaries and dependency direction
findings.description:
- No Python, no installer, manifest or dispatcher change.
- Preflight, provenance and gap markers are consumed from 361 unchanged.
- Interview, candidates and routing are left to 363, 364 and 366.
- Dependencies (`[361]`) and provided interfaces (363, 364) match the plan.

findings.title: Slice plan success criteria and open question covered
findings.description:
- All four required sections (hotspots, entry points, layers, dependencies) are present with named source fields.
- Entry points, which 361 omitted, are sourced from the `entry-point` tag, not a filename heuristic.
- The `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` reuse question and `[INFERRED]` governance are decided with reasons.
- The three 361 deferrals (`config.json`, `.understandignore`, `analyzedFiles`) are closed.

findings.title: Failure modes for new reads are enumerated
findings.description:
- Each section has an explicit fallback.
- Walkthrough steps 5 and 6 exercise the gap-marker paths (empty tour, missing tag, missing `meta.json`) and the count-discrepancy path.
- A `nodeIds` entry resolving to a function or class node is reported as drift, not silently filtered.
- The parent architecture states no NFRs for this path.

Closing observations are an unmarked-inference path
Claims about the 361 skill text are not verifiable from the documents
